capabilities.text: Type a linear rule in x, such as y = 2x + 1, and every y is worked out for the x-values
capabilities.note: The opening state is y = 2x + 1.

capabilities.text: Type a rule with powers of x, such as y = x^2 or y = x^2 − 3
capabilities.note: From the bullet and the Values help.

capabilities.text: Type an exponential rule, such as y = 3(2)^x or y = 2^x
capabilities.note: Bullet; example 'Table of values for the exponential function y = 2ˣ'.

capabilities.text: Type a trigonometric rule, such as y = sin x
capabilities.note: Bullet. Pairs with the π and degree x-values in cap-02e/02f.; control, not core (owner, scope review 2026-11-19)

capabilities.text: Type a rule with x in the denominator, such as y = 1/x
capabilities.note: From the About text, not the bullets. Where it has no value see cap-04f.; control, not core (owner, scope review 2026-11-19)

capabilities.text: Pick Typed and type the x and y pairs yourself, one pair per row, with no rule
capabilities.note: Example 'Pattern table' uses source=typed with one row per pair.

capabilities.text: Type words, not only numbers, in a typed table's cells
capabilities.note: Bullet: 'words too'; About: 'numbers or words, for a pattern or a table with no rule'.

capabilities.text: Paste the pairs from a spreadsheet, one pair per row
capabilities.note: Bullet: 'typed or pasted one per row'.

capabilities.text: Set the x-values as a range with From, To and Step
capabilities.note: Opening state: From −2, To 2, Step 1 (five columns).

capabilities.text: Set the x-values as a list, such as −2, 0, 1/2, 3, with uneven gaps
capabilities.note: Example 'Input-output table' uses the list 1, 2, 3, 5, 10.

capabilities.text: Type the range or list with fractions (a step of 1/2) and the x-values are written as fractions
capabilities.note: Example 'y = x/2 + 1': x is 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2 written as stacked fractions.

capabilities.text: Type a decimal step such as 0.5 and the x-values are written as decimals
capabilities.note: FAQ: 'Type x-values like 1/2 or a step of 0.5'. That the x-values are then written as decimals is inferred, not seen.

capabilities.text: Type the range or list in multiples of π and the x-values are written with π
capabilities.note: Bullet and Values help. A trig rule then reads x in radians (inferred).

capabilities.text: Type the range or list in degrees (0, 30°, 90°) and the x-values are written with °, the rule reading them as degrees
capabilities.note: Values help: 'Type the range in fractions, π or degrees (0, 30°, 90°) and the x-values are written that way.'

capabilities.text: Leave a chosen y value blank for students
capabilities.note: Example 'Complete the table for y = 2x + 1' blanks y for x = 1 and x = 3 (blank=y3,y5). On the figure the action is cap-i01.

capabilities.text: Leave a chosen x value blank for students, so they find the input
capabilities.note: The opening state has a click handle on every x cell: 'x in column 1: click to make a blank'. On the figure the action is cap-i02.

capabilities.text: Blank every y at once with one button
capabilities.note: Button 'Blank every y' under Values. Example 'y = x/2 + 1' blanks y0 to y4.

capabilities.text: Leave a cell empty in a typed table and it prints as a blank
capabilities.note: Example 'Pattern table': figures 4 and 10 have no tile count.

capabilities.text: List each blank with its value as the answer key, worded with the headings ("y when x = 1: 3", "Output when Input = 5: 13")
capabilities.note: From the About text and the FAQ: 'Each blank and its value is listed under the table for your answer key.' Wording seen on the example pages.; counts when drawn on the figure's key copy (Show answers on) (owner, scope review 2026-11-19)

capabilities.text: Say whether a table from a rule is linear and give its rate of change ("Linear: the rate of change is 2.")
capabilities.note: About: 'says whether the table is linear and its rate of change, so the answer key is ready too'. The wording for a table that is not linear was not seen.; counts when drawn on the figure's key copy (Show answers on) (owner, scope review 2026-11-19); covers saying "not linear" too

capabilities.text: For typed pairs that are linear, give the line they follow and its rate of change ("Linear: y = 3x + 2, a rate of change of 3.")
capabilities.note: FAQ: 'the settings panel says whether they are linear and gives the line they follow'. Seen on the 'Pattern table' example.; counts when drawn on the figure's key copy (Show answers on) (owner, scope review 2026-11-19)

capabilities.text: When the rule above the table is a blank line, give the rule in the answer key ("The rule: y = 3x − 2")
capabilities.note: Seen on the 'Input-output table: find the rule' example.; counts when drawn on the figure's key copy (Show answers on) (owner, scope review 2026-11-19)

capabilities.text: Write worked-out values that are whole numbers or fractions exactly, fractions in lowest terms
capabilities.note: 'Worked-out values as' defaults to Fractions. The examples write fractions stacked (5/4, 3/2).

capabilities.text: Write worked-out values as decimals instead of fractions
capabilities.note: 'Worked-out values as: Decimals'.

capabilities.text: Round values to whole numbers
capabilities.note: 'Round the rest to' option 0, 'Whole numbers'.

capabilities.text: Round values to 1, 2, 3 or 4 decimal places
capabilities.note: 'Round the rest to' options 1 to 4; 2 decimal places is the opening state.

capabilities.text: With Fractions chosen, round values that are not fractions (such as √2 or sin 1) to the chosen places and keep the fractions exact
capabilities.note: The Numbers summary at the opening state reads 'Fractions, else 2 decimal places'. FAQ: 'Values that are not fractions, like the square root of 2, are rounded to the places you choose.'

capabilities.text: Write "undefined" where the rule has no value (1/x at x = 0)
capabilities.note: Bullet: 'where the rule has no value, undefined'.

capabilities.text: Use the headings Input and Output
capabilities.note: Heading pairs: x / y (opening state), Input / Output, x / f(x), n / aₙ.

capabilities.text: Use the headings x and f(x)
Use the headings n and aₙ for a sequence
capabilities.note: From the page's Heading pairs, not the bullets.

capabilities.text: Type your own first heading (for x), such as Figure number
capabilities.note: Example 'Pattern table': xHeading=Figure number.

capabilities.text: Type your own second heading (for y), such as Number of tiles
capabilities.note: Example 'Pattern table': yHeading=Number of tiles.

capabilities.text: Leave a heading empty so it prints as a blank for students
capabilities.note: The heading boxes' placeholder: 'Leave empty for a blank'. From the controls, not the bullets.

capabilities.text: Write a table title as text
capabilities.note: Table title: Text / Blank line / None; None is the opening state.

capabilities.text: Put a blank line in place of the table title for students
Write the rule above the table
capabilities.note: 'The rule, above the table': None (opening state) / Written / Blank line.

capabilities.text: Put a blank line in place of the rule above the table, so students find the rule
capabilities.note: Example 'Input-output table': 'under a blank line after y = for the rule'. FAQ: find-the-rule question.

capabilities.text: Run the table down in two columns (a T-chart) instead of across in two rows
capabilities.note: 'The table runs': Across (opening state) / Down.

capabilities.text: Use plain headings instead of gray ones
capabilities.note: 'Headings': Gray (opening state) / Plain.

capabilities.text: Make the labels large
capabilities.note: Label size buttons on the figure toolbar: Large / Medium (opening state) / Small.

capabilities.text: Make the labels small
Click a y value on the figure to make it a blank
capabilities.note: From the Values help and the opening state's handles: 'y for x = −2: click to make a blank'.

capabilities.text: Click an x value on the figure to make it a blank
capabilities.note: From the opening state's handles: 'x in column 1: click to make a blank'. The bullets name only 'any value'.

capabilities.text: Click a blank on the figure to fill its value back in
capabilities.note: Inferred, not seen: a toggle is the likely reading, but the browser here could not run the page to confirm it.
